Commentary.Commentary: That's it from the Karachi leg. We now move to Lahore for the remaining games of the series. The 5th T20I is on 28th September (Wednesday) at 8 pm IST (2.30 pm GMT), but you can join us in advance for the build-up. Until then, it's goodbye and cheers!

Babar Azam, the captain of Pakistan, starts by saying that the way they started with the bat, they were 10-15 runs short. He praises the cameo of Asif Ali and then the efforts of the bowling group. Mentions that they keep the middle order flexible. Regarding Haris Rauf's bowling, Babar replies that he is getting better day by day and calls him the leading bowler of Pakistan.

Moeen Ali, the captain of England, says that it was an amazing game of cricket and it kept swinging both ways. Adds that they should have chased it down but they lost a lot of wickets in the Powerplay. Praises Liam Dawson for his knock and tells that he had a brilliant all-round game. Feels that they should have won with 9 runs needed off 12 balls but credits Pakistan for getting over the line.

Haris Rauf (4-0-32-3) is the Player of the Match. The speedster says that this win will give confidence to the team. Shares that his plan was not to give up and pick the wickets in the penultimate over. Mentions that you need to handle pressure in international cricket and he tries to give his best.
Stay tuned for the presentation...

Earlier in the evening, Pakistan batted well in the first half but lacked the killer instinct in the last 10 overs. As a result, they ended with a below-par total. But the bowling efforts of Mohammad Nawaz and Haris Rauf earned them a series-levelling win. If we leave alone Hasnain's last over, he too was very impressive.

England were at the door of victory but Haris Rauf closed it on their face with an exceptional penultimate over. He removed Liam Dawson and Olly Stone off consecutive deliveries and conceded only 5 runs. With 4 needed off the last over and one wicket in hand, the visitors were dragged away from the winning line after getting so close. A very pleasing win for the home team as they kept fighting till the end.

The chase was full of twists and turns. Pakistan pegged back England in the Powerplay but Harry Brook stitched a couple of stands, one with Ben Duckett and another with Moeen Ali to keep the touring team in the game. When he departed, England needed 54 off 34 balls and the writing appeared to be on the wall. But when you bat deep, you always have that extra arrow in your quiver to target the enemy. Brook gone, Moeen gone, Willey gone, no issues. Liam Dawson flexed his muscles with a handy cameo to take this game deep. He targeted the 18th over bowled by Mohammad Hasnain and amassed 24 runs from it to bring down the equation to 9 off 12 balls.
Phew! What a thriller! Pakistan have crossed the line eventually much to the delight of the capacity crowd. Finally, we got a close match and this win for the home team has levelled the series 2-2.

OUT! RUN OUT! The bails lit-up and so does the crowd! A stunning comeback from Pakistan. It is a length ball, on off. Reece Topley stays back and defends it towards short mid-wicket. He takes off towards the other end. Shan Masood is quick to get to the ball, he dives forward and under-arms the ball at the non-striker's end to score a direct hit. Pakistan know they have got their man. The replays later confirm that Reece Topley is miles away from the crease. The big screen shows out. PAKISTAN WIN THE GAME BY 3 RUNS.
Good length, on off. Reece Topley defends it solidly towards covers. Adil Rashid ventures out looking for a single but he is sent back and rightly so.
Mohammad Wasim to bowl the final over. 4 needed off 6 balls.
A length ball, outside off. Adil Rashid looks to drive it away but misses. It zips past the outside edge.

NOT OUT! A rip-roaring yorker, toe-crusher around leg, Reece Topley fails to dig it out and is hit on the back leg. They appeal but nothing from the umpire. Babar takes the referral. Ball Tracking finds that it has pitched outside leg.
Appeal for an lbw, not given. Haris Rauf convinces his skipper to take the referral. Pitching outside leg! No hat-trick for Rauf.
Reece Topley is the number 11 batter. Rauf on a hat-trick.

OUT! SOUND OF TIMBER! Haris Rauf comes up with a rocket and has picked two in two. Hurls across a length ball, around off, skidding off the surface, Stone stands there like a stone, trying to keep it out but is beaten for excess pace. The stumps are disturbed. The entire stadium erupts in joy.
Debutant Olly Stone joins Rashid in the middle. 5 needed off 9 balls.

OUT! CAUGHT! Haris Rauf strikes and sends back Liam Dawson. Pakistan would be really happy to see his back. Back of a length again, on middle. Liam Dawson looks to go for the pull shot but does not connect well. It lobs towards mid-wicket. The substitute fielder, Mohammad Haris moves to his right and takes the simplest of catches.
Commentary.Howout: c sub Mohammad Haris b Haris Rauf

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Liam Dawson is running away with the game here. It is a short ball, on the bodyline. Liam Dawson swivels on the back foot and hooks it over mid-wicket. The fielder in the deep sprints to his left but is unable to keep the ball in play.
Good length, in the channel. It is very close for Liam Dawson to cut away. It takes the inside edge, bounces and goes to the keeper.

A single to end the over! An expensive one for Pakistan. This over has certainly turned the scenario of the game. 24 runs come off it. It is a full ball, on off. Liam Dawson pushes it to extra cover and scampers across for a quick single.
A length ball, on off. Liam Dawson steps outside the crease and blocks it back to the bowler watchfully.
FOUR! No one in the crowd can believe what they are seeing here. It is full, drifting down leg. Liam Dawson stays back and flicks it down to deep square leg for four more.
FOUR! Put away with ease. The required rate is under 6 now. Short in length and outside off, Liam Dawson stays back and ramps it over short third man.

FOUR! Liam Dawson is on fire. He makes the most of the Free Hit here! Liam Dawson goes down leg, and Hasnain follows him with a full delivery. Liam Dawson wrists it towards the cow corner. One bounce and over the ropes.

NO BALL AND FOUR! It is all happening here for England. Top placement from Liam Dawson. He is shutting up the crowd here. It is a good-length ball, outside off. Liam Dawson waits for it and steers it past short third man. It races away to the fence. The umpire signals a NO BALL to add salt to the wounds as the bowler oversteps.
SIX! ALL THE WAY! It is overpitched, on middle. Liam Dawson gets under it and smokes it over the long off fence for a maximum. Is there a twist in the tale?
It is full, on leg. Adil Rashid shuffles and flicks it behind square on the leg side. The batters take two with ease.
Very full this time, on off. Liam Dawson defends it to covers and crosses for a single.
Good single! A length ball, shaping in from outside off. Adil Rashid stays back and defends it to his right. Liam Dawson is quick to charge to the other end. They get a single.
Adil Rashid is in next. 37 needed off 21 balls.

OUT! TIMBER! Haris Rauf has the last laugh here. The crowd has gone berserk. David Willey's cameo comes to an end. Haris Rauf comes 'round the wicket and fires in a yorker, right in the blockhole. David Willey is stuck inside his crease. He looks to keep it out but is a bit late. The ball goes through and shatters the stumps behind. Big celebration from Rauf!

FOUR! Consecutive boundaries now for Willey. He is turning the game on its head here. It is a length ball, on middle and leg. David Willey shuffles across and gives it the same treatment just like the previous delivery. Guess what? The result is the same. Another boundary at third man.
FOUR! A much-needed boundary! This should ease some pressure. It is a slower ball, on a length, around middle. Willey shuffles and scoops it over the keeper's head for a boundary.

David Willey is on the ground as he somehow manages to dig out a yorker, nailed onto his pads. The batters cross for one. An excellent over from Mohammad Hasnain comes to an end. Just 6 runs off it. England need 45 runs off 24 balls now.
Second dot of the over! It is full, swinging away a bit late. David Willey gets it back to the bowler off the toe end.

LEG BYE! Mohammad Hasnain attacking the pads yet again, fuller in length. Liam Dawson isn't offered much room. He looks to flick it away but misses. The ball rolls to the leg side off the pads. They collect a leg bye.
A precious dot now! A full toss, around waist height, into the right-hander. Liam Dawson goes back and looks to heave it across the line. He misses and takes a hit on his thigh pads.
Fuller, on middle and leg, Liam Dawson tucks it through the gap at mid on. The batters take two more.
It is full, angled into the pads. Liam Dawson whips it towards mid on. The fielder is placed at long on which gives enough time for the batters to take a couple.
Mohammad Hasnain is back on. 2 for 11 in his two overs so far.
Outside off, dabbed down to point for one.
A mistimed drive to mid off and Willey picks up a run.
A bit of reverse swing there. Full and around leg, Willey tries to flick but ends up pushing it back to the bowler.
Fuller on middle, worked to mid-wicket for a single.
Liam Dawson walks in next.

OUT! Brook holes out! The celebration from the crowd shows that this is a body blow to England. Short in length, around middle and leg, Brook again stays leg-side to this one and swings his bat at it. This time the connection is not good enough to clear fine leg and Mohammad Hasnain takes a safe catch near the fence. 54 needed off 34 balls and England are now down to their all-rounders.
Commentary.Howout: c Mohammad Hasnain b Mohammad Wasim

Commentary.Commentary: Wide! Spears a full ball way down the leg side, Brook tries flicking but misses. Good diving take from Rizwan.
FOUR! Short and around middle, angling in, Brook makes room for himself and pulls it to deep square leg for a boundary. 55 needed off 35 balls.
Quicker again, around off, defended back to the bowler.
Flatter one, around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Shortish and on off, it's wristed down to long on for a run.
Quicker and on middle, punched down to long on for one.
David Willey is the new batter.

OUT! BOWLED! The crowd comes back to life. Nawaz drags his length a bit short, lands it around off and gets it to spin back into the batter. Moeen gives the charge and attempts to heave it over the leg side but misses. The stumps are shattered and Nawaz gets his third wicket. 61 needed off 40 balls.
Flighted and on off, Brook uses his feet and strokes it to long off for a single.
Mohammad Nawaz to bowl out. 2 for 32 so far.
Fuller and on off, Brook makes room and drives it to sweeper cover for one. 9 from the over!
Short around off, punched in front of square on the off side for a single.
FOUR! Smashed! Fuller and around middle, Moeen steps back to make room and smashes it over extra cover for a boundary.
Very full and around off, Brook drives it back and Ahmed only manages to deflect it behind to long off. A single is taken.
Slightly short around off, Ali goes on the back foot and forces it down to long on for one.
Fuller and on middle, drilled back to the bowler who failed to stop it and they crossed.
FOUR! Fine shot! Short again from Rauf, outside off, Moeen stands back to fetch it from there and swings it behind square leg for a boundary. 71 needed off 48 balls.
Excellent stop in the deep! Rauf delivers a short ball around off, Moeen pulls it in front of square on the leg side. Mohammad Wasim makes a stop near the fence and saves two.
Follows the batter down the leg side with a full ball, Brook clips it behind square leg and takes a single.
Slower again, a bit short and on off, Moeen steers it through point and rotates the strike.
Short and on middle at 139 kph, Brook goes on the leg side this time and hammers it to deep square leg for a run.
Play and a miss! Slower one, on a length around leg, Brook steps back to loft it down the ground with a straight bat but fails to connect.
Haris Rauf is back on.
Fuller and on middle, pushed back to the bowler. A dot ball to end a quick over.
Again it's on the shorter side around off, Brook moves back and pushes it down to long on for a run.
Shortish and on off, punched through covers for a single.
Fires it short and around off at 101 kph, Brook stays back and forces it to long on for one.
Quicker and around leg, Moeen eases it towards mid on for one as the bowler himself chases it down.
Flatter and on middle, worked through mid-wicket for a single.

Drinks break. It's been a high-octane chase so far. England have lost wickets but they are trying their best to keep the required rate under control. The current partnership holds the key for them. Pakistan have done well with the ball in the first half but it's crucial they maintain the same intensity from here on. 85 needed off 60 balls - we are heading to a tight finish.
Fuller again, around leg, Brook wrists it through mid-wicket for a single. 19 from the over!
Fuller and outside off, Ali pushes it to sweeper cover for a run.

SIX! This has been nailed! England just keep coming at you, regardless of how many wickets they lose. Floated and full, around off, Moeen shimmies down the track and launches it over long on. 87 needed off 62 balls.
FOUR! 11 from the first three balls of this over. Fuller and around leg, Moeen goes down and sweeps it sweetly to the deep square leg fence.
Arm ball, around middle and leg, Brook tries to work it on the leg side but gets an inside edge. It deflects off his pads to the off side and they cross.

SIX! What a shot! Loopy and full, around off and turning away a bit, Harry Brook advances down the track and with a lovely extension of his arms, he lofts it nonchalantly over extra cover. Special talent.
Serves it flat and on middle, Brook turns it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Fires it in, on middle and leg, Moeen eases it to long on for a single.
Fuller and on off, driven back to the bowler.
Flatter and on off, punched to covers.
Helps it to mid-wicket for a single.

Mishit! Flighted and outside off, a bit on the shorter side and holding off the surface too, Moeen hangs back and plays a mistimed lofted shot over covers. They cross for a run, Moeen wants another run but is sent back. He gets in safely with a dive. The throw comes to the bowler who tries to collect it and tumbles over Moeen in the process.

'Catch it' is the shout but it has not carried back to the bowler. Full and floated on middle, Harry skips down the track and drives it back. It's a bit aerial but safe as Nawaz stops it to his right. End of a superb over.
Wide! Skidding down the leg side, Brook tries to flick but misses.
Fuller and on middle, worked through wide mid on for a run.
And again! Arm ball outside off, quicker through the air, Moeen plays for the spin and is beaten.
Beaten! Arm ball outside off, going straight on, Moeen pushes inside the line and misses.
Moeen Ali walks in next.

OUT! Given lbw! Duckett has decided to review the decision. Coming to the delivery - It's a flighted one, full and around off, spinning in a shade, Ben Duckett goes down and across to sweep but misses. He is pinged on the front pad, they appeal and the umpire raises his finger. DRS time. Nothing on the UltraEdge. The Ball Tracking finds everything in line. Three reds and the crowd is delighted. A big breakthrough as Ben Duckett has been a nuisance for the home team in this series. 110 needed off 76 balls.
Flatter and on the pads, Duckett nudges it in front of square leg and scampers back for the second run.
Mohammad Nawaz is back into the attack. 1 for 9 in his 1 over so far.
That misses the off pole by a whisker! Flighted and full, around off, Brook attempts to reverse paddle it but misses. Rizwan has his hands on his head.
Quicker on off, Ben knocks it down to long on and rotates the strike.
Walks down the track and pushes it defensively down to long on. Brook gets a single.
Skidding down the leg side, it's eased behind square leg for a single.
Skidding in from outside off, Ben tries to play the reverse sweep but misses. The bowler appeals for an lbw but the impact was outside off.
Flatter and shorter on off, Duckett cuts it to deep point and collects two. The umpire gets it checked if it was one short but Ben Duckett had dragged his bat in while turning for the second run.
Iftikhar Ahmed comes into the attack. Babar Azam is forced to hold back Usman Qadir here as the current pair has played the leggie very well in the last two games.

FOUR! Pierces the gap! A low full toss on middle, Brook steps back to make room and drills it through covers for a boundary. At the end of the Powerplay, England are 50 for 3. 117 needed off 84 balls.
Shortish and on off, Duckett punches it to the right side of mid off for a single.
Drifting down the leg side, Brook fails to flick and is hit on the pads. It rolls to square leg and they collect a leg bye.
Full and on the pads, Ben helps it to deep square leg and rotates the strike.
On middle, flicked to deep square leg for one.

DROPPED! Mohammad Nawaz drops a sitter. Fuller in length around off, Harry Brook slices his drive to covers where Nawaz reacts to his right, tries to reverse cup it but fails. Harry is the batter in form and this could be a costly miss.
Change. Haris Rauf to bowl the final over of the Powerplay.

FOUR! Another mishit but it's again a boundary down the ground. Short and outside off, Duckett rocks back to pull it across the line but it comes off the toe end and flies behind the bowler. Again the mid on fielder chases but in vain. 15 from the over!
FOUR! Not from the middle of the bat but it races away. Fuller and outside off, Ben Duckett forces it down the ground and finds the fence as the mid on fielder chases.
FOUR! Boom! Back of a length, around middle, Duckett stands still inside the crease and heaves it over wide mid on for a boundary.
Fuller around leg, at 140 clicks again, Harry tries to flick but fails to middle it properly. It deflects to square leg and they cross.
On a length, around middle, at 140 clicks, Ben Duckett works it wide of mid-wicket and rotates the strike.
Angles in a length ball on middle, at 137 kph, Brook tickles it in front of square leg and takes a single.

FOUR! Superb execution! Back of a length, around leg and following the batter at 144 clicks, Duckett does well to create some room for himself as he guides it through the gap between backward point and short third man.
Yorker around leg at 145 kph, Ben gets back and digs it out at the last moment.
Play and a miss! A sharp delivery, on a shortish length around off at 142 clicks, Ben Duckett jumps across the stumps to play the paddle scoop but misses.
Lovely piece of fielding! Back of a length and outside off, Brook uses the pace and guides it down to third man. Wasim dives near the fence and saves three runs for his side.
Extra bounce from a good length around leg, Ben tries to glance but it takes the upper half of his blade. It goes uppishly to square leg but falls safely as they cross.
A length delivery around leg, Duckett helps it off his pads to mid-wicket.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and pushes it back past the bowler. They steal a quick run as the mid on fielder mops it up.
On a length and outside off, Ben taps it down to cover-point and screams a loud no.
Angles in a length ball on middle, Brook nudges it to square leg for a run.
Around middle and leg, on a length, Duckett works it through square leg and takes a single.
Beaten! The crowd roars again. It's involved big time. A 142 kph delivery, short and outside off, Ben flashes his bat at it but fails to connect.
FOUR! Shot! Short in length and outside off, angling away, Ben Duckett stays back and slaps it past the backward point fielder for a boundary.
Harry Brook walks in next. 153 needed. Here comes Mohammad Wasim...

OUT! BOWLED! The crowd is going bonkers at the National Stadium. Hasnain is on fire. He dishes out a length ball around middle, at 146 kph, Will Jacks stays back to hit it across the line but misses. It goes on to clip one of the bails and England lose their third wicket inside the Powerplay.
Serves it on a length and outside off, Jacks pushes it with an angled bat to point.
Short and around leg, Ben pulls it through square leg and gets off the mark with a single.
A length ball around leg, slower in pace, Duckett defends it to the off side.
Ben Duckett is in next.

OUT! A stunning catch from Usman Qadir! Back of a length, around middle and leg at 142 kph, Hales is cramped for room and plays it away from the upper half of his bat. It flies to the left of mid-wicket where Usman Qadir dives across to his left and takes a ripper of a catch. Superb effort, just the kind you need to lift the confidence of the entire team. The crowd is roaring. England are under early pressure. 154 needed off 112 balls.
Commentary.Howout: c Usman Qadir b Mohammad Hasnain

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Nicely played! Short in length around middle, Hales waits for it and pulls it past the mid-wicket fielder for a boundary.
Mohammad Hasnain to bowl from the opposite end.
Quicker and shorter on off, Jacks punches it from the back foot to covers. End of an eventful first over.
Flatter arm ball on middle, skidding in, Hales hangs back and nudges it to square leg for one.
Will Jacks is the number 3 batter.

OUT! CAUGHT! This one is a well-planned wicket. Loopy delivery, full and on middle, Salt once again sits down to play the slog sweep but he has played that towards deep mid-wicket. There is a fielder positioned for this shot and Mohammad Wasim makes no mistake near the fence. Mohammad Nawaz strikes and draws first blood.
Commentary.Howout: c Mohammad Wasim b Mohammad Nawaz

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Salt has come out with intent! Fuller and around leg, Philip Salt kneels down and powers it over square leg for a boundary.
Flighted and full, around off, it's pushed back to the bowler.
FOUR! England start well! Nawaz drops it short and around off, Salt steps back to make room and whacks it through covers for a cracking boundary.
